title: MCP4SAS is for Perl and Python users
lines: Choose either runner; the SAS program stays the same.
Both can submit SAS, handle files and return logs.
narration: You don't have to be a Perl programmer to use MCP4SAS. Python users have their own runner, beside the Perl version. These two commands submit the same SAS program. Choose either one. Your SAS code and reusable macros stay in SAS; the runner handles the connection, files and results.

title: Windows: run Python directly in Cygwin
lines: After Quick Setup, use Cygwin in your MCP4SAS folder.
The runner finds the installed project SASPy environment.
Save test.sas first; no manual environment activation is needed.
narration: Stay in the Cygwin terminal opened in your MCP4SAS folder. Once installation and SAS configuration are complete, just type python, followed by the runner and your code or saved file. The runner finds the project's compatible SASPy environment automatically. There is no separate activation command to copy. You still need your SAS account, Java, and the encryption files downloaded from SAS. If setup is incomplete, follow the runner's diagnostic message before retrying.

title: macOS and Ubuntu: the same simple commands
lines: Complete the platform installer and SAS configuration first.
Run from the MCP4SAS folder; reuse its compatible Python environment.
narration: On a Mac or Ubuntu, finish the platform installer shown earlier, then use python three for the same commands. Run them from the MCP4SAS folder. The runner can reuse a compatible project environment, so you don't need to activate it for each submission. The separate Python guide is available if you want a native Python-only installation. Your SAS account and encryption-file requirements stay the same.

title: Save test.sas; choose either runner
lines: Save the file with Ctrl+S before submitting it.
Use the same runtime and session name when reusing WORK tables.
narration: Remember the saved-file example from earlier? Python users simply choose the matching dot-py runner. Save test dot sass before submitting it, and check that your terminal is in the right folder. You can run either command without an AI assistant. When reusing a named SAS session, stay with the same runtime; Perl and Python keep separate session registries.

title: The same scientific examples in both languages
lines: The original SAS macros and datasets are reused.
narration: The scientific examples have Python counterparts too. Choose either command for the expression clustergram, or the regional plot comparing several genome-wide association studies. Both routes reuse the original SAS programs, macros and input data. They also collect the figures and numerical tables. You aren't asking an AI model to invent a replacement plot.

title: Use an AI agent with the Python server
lines: stdio: the MCP client starts server.py.
The current 0.1.5 plugin keeps its Perl setup.
narration: For AI-assisted work, the Python edition has its own MCP server. A client can launch it over standard input and output, or connect to the loopback HTTP endpoint shown here. Use one transport, not both commands at once. The Python guide shows the separate client configuration. The existing extension still uses Perl; installing the Python files doesn't silently change your assistant's connection.

title: Check the figures, numerical tables and SAS log
lines: Replace PATH_TO_RESULTS with your actual output folder.
Perl or Python: keep the SAS log and inspect the returned figure.
narration: Use the matching checker to verify the downloaded files and numerical results. Replace the placeholder with your actual results folder, and read the complete SAS log, including warnings. Automated checks don't replace scientific interpretation or a visual review. Whether you prefer Perl or Python, MCP4SAS gives you a repeatable route from saved SAS code to results. The links below take you to both sets of examples.
